category: Category B — Tenant and Landlord Disputes
name: Refusal to provide itemized deduction statement
expected: Explains that deductions require verified bills/receipts; tenant can challenge arbitrary deductions.
prompt: Landlord deducted ₹20,000 but refuses to give receipts or bills for the alleged repairs.
raw_response:
I understand how frustrating and unfair it is when a landlord makes large deductions from your deposit without providing any bills or receipts for the repairs.

### | Your Situation
You are a tenant facing an issue where your landlord has withheld ₹20,000 from your security deposit for alleged repairs without providing any bills, receipts, or valid proof of expenditure. The property is located in India, and the landlord is refusing transparency regarding these deductions.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under Section 108(m) and (o) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a tenant is only responsible for returning the property in as good condition as it was received, subject to reasonable wear and tear. A landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage or standard maintenance without a contractual basis and verifiable proof.
- Principles under the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (and general principles of contract and property law in India) dictate that security deposits must be refunded upon vacating, minus only legitimate, agreed-upon deductions substantiated by actual bills or repair estimates.
- Arbitrarily withholding funds without accounting for them can amount to an unfair trade practice or breach of the lease agreement.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence, including your lease agreement, bank statements showing the deposit payment, move-in and move-out photographs of the property condition, and all written communication or chat logs with the landlord regarding the ₹20,000 deduction.
2. Send a written demand notice to the landlord granting 15 days to either provide genuine bills and receipts for the repairs or refund the entire withheld amount of ₹20,000.
3. If the landlord fails to comply within the notice period, you may approach the appropriate Rent Authority or Consumer Commission depending on your state's local tenancy enactments and dispute resolution framework.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
1. Did you sign a written lease agreement, and does it contain any specific clauses about maintenance, painting, or security deposit deductions?
2. What is the city or state where this rented property is located?

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.

citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.
